sections.heading: Retinal Conditions: Diseases of the Light-Sensing Layer

items: The retina is the thin layer of light-sensitive neural tissue lining the back of the eye — essentially an extension of the brain that converts focused light into electrical signals transmitted to the brain via the optic nerve. Retinal diseases are among the most vision-threatening because the retina has limited capacity for regeneration. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

In Palamu: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) affects the macula — the central, most visually critical part of the retina responsible for reading, face recognition, and fine detail. Dry AMD involves progressive atrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium and photoreceptors; wet AMD involves abnormal blood vessel growth under the macula that leaks fluid and causes rapid central vision loss.

Diabetic retinopathy, the leading cause of preventable blindness in working-age adults, results from chronic high blood sugar damaging retinal capillaries, causing leakage (macular edema), vessel closure (ischemia), and abnormal new vessel growth (proliferative retinopathy).
Retinal detachment — where the retina separates from its underlying blood supply — is a surgical emergency requiring urgent repair with vitrectomy, scleral buckling, or pneumatic retinopexy.
Retinal vein occlusion (branch or central) causes sudden vision loss from blockage of venous outflow.
Macular hole is a full-thickness defect in the central retina causing a blind spot in central vision, treated with vitrectomy and gas tamponade.
Epiretinal membrane (macular pucker) is a thin layer of scar tissue on the macular surface that contracts and wrinkles the retina, causing metamorphopsia.
Retinitis pigmentosa is a group of inherited retinal dystrophies where rod photoreceptors progressively degenerate.

Dr. Dibya Prabha, with fellowship training in retina at LV Prasad Eye Institute Hyderabad, provides specialized diagnosis and treatment for the full spectrum of retinal diseases at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care.

The cornea is the transparent, dome-shaped front surface of the eye — the most powerful refractive element, accounting for approximately two-thirds of the eye's focusing power. Corneal conditions directly degrade the optical quality of the eye. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

In Palamu: Keratitis — infection or inflammation of the cornea — can be bacterial (especially in contact lens wearers — Pseudomonas and Staphylococcus), viral (herpes simplex — the leading cause of infectious corneal blindness), fungal (Fusarium, Aspergillus — associated with vegetative trauma), or Acanthamoeba (a protozoan in contact lens wearers exposed to tap water). Keratitis is an ophthalmological emergency because it can perforate the cornea within 24 to 48 hours.
Keratoconus is a progressive, non-inflammatory thinning and conical deformation of the cornea causing irregular astigmatism and vision loss — strongly associated with chronic eye rubbing and atopy.
Corneal dystrophies (Fuchs endothelial dystrophy, lattice dystrophy, granular dystrophy) are inherited conditions causing progressive corneal clouding.

Dry eye syndrome, the most common ocular surface disorder, involves tear film instability, hyperosmolarity, and inflammation — it is not simply a lack of tears but a complex disease requiring systematic management.
Pterygium is a fleshy, wing-shaped growth of conjunctival tissue onto the cornea, associated with chronic UV exposure, that can obstruct vision and cause astigmatism.
Corneal abrasions and recurrent erosion syndrome cause acute, intense pain and photophobia — the cornea has the highest density of sensory nerve endings of any tissue.
Dr. Dibya Prabha evaluates the cornea and anterior segment using slit lamp biomicroscopy with fluorescein staining at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care.

sections.heading: Lens Conditions: Cataract and Lens Disorders

items: The crystalline lens sits behind the iris and focuses light onto the retina, with the ability to change shape (accommodation) for near focusing — a capacity that progressively declines with age (presbyopia). Cataract — clouding of the crystalline lens — is the most common cause of reversible blindness worldwide and the most frequently performed surgery globally. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

In Palamu: Age-related cataract is nearly universal in older adults and comes in three main types: nuclear sclerotic (central lens hardening and yellowing), cortical (spoke-like peripheral opacities), and posterior subcapsular (plaque at the back of the lens, causing disproportionate glare and difficulty reading and driving at night).

Cataracts also result from diabetes (sorbitol pathway activation), prolonged corticosteroid use (topical, oral, inhaled, or injected), ocular trauma, previous intraocular surgery, radiation exposure, and congenital factors (rubella, metabolic disorders).

The definitive treatment is phacoemulsification with intraocular lens (IOL) implantation — a 15- to 30-minute outpatient procedure performed under topical anesthesia with a success rate exceeding 98 percent.

Modern premium IOLs include: aspheric IOLs (improved contrast sensitivity), toric IOLs (correct astigmatism), multifocal and extended depth of focus IOLs (reduce spectacle dependence for near and intermediate vision), and blue-light filtering IOLs.
Ectopia lentis — dislocation of the lens from its normal position — occurs in Marfan syndrome (upward dislocation), homocystinuria (downward dislocation), and trauma.
Dr. Dibya Prabha performs comprehensive cataract evaluation at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care with optical biometry (IOL Master) for precise IOL power calculation.

sections.heading: Glaucoma: The Silent Thief of Sight

items: Glaucoma is a group of optic neuropathies characterized by progressive degeneration of retinal ganglion cells, resulting in a characteristic pattern of optic nerve head cupping and visual field loss. It is the second leading cause of blindness worldwide and the leading cause of irreversible blindness — because the vision loss cannot be restored. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.
The major types include: At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

In Palamu: Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) — the most common form, where the drainage angle is open but the trabecular meshwork is dysfunctional, causing elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) and gradual, asymptomatic peripheral vision loss.

Angle-closure glaucoma (acute and chronic) — where the peripheral iris blocks the trabecular meshwork, acutely (a painful, red eye with rock-hard IOP and a mid-dilated pupil — an ophthalmological emergency) or chronically (asymptomatic progressive angle closure).

Normal-tension glaucoma — optic nerve damage and visual field loss despite IOP within the normal range, associated with vascular dysregulation, nocturnal hypotension, and possibly impaired CSF pressure.
Secondary glaucomas — resulting from uveitis, steroid use, trauma, neovascularization (in diabetic retinopathy or vein occlusion), or pigment dispersion.

Risk factors include: elevated IOP (the only modifiable risk factor), age over 60, family history (first-degree relative increases risk 4- to 9-fold), African or Hispanic ancestry, high myopia, and thin central corneal thickness (which causes IOP to be underestimated). At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

Treatment — medications (prostaglandin analogs, beta-blockers, alpha-agonists, carbonic anhydrase inhibitors), laser (selective laser trabeculoplasty for POAG, laser peripheral iridotomy for angle-closure), and surgery (trabeculectomy, drainage implants) — is aimed at lowering IOP, the only proven disease-modifying intervention. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

content.title: Critical public health message
content.text: Because POAG is asymptomatic until advanced, regular comprehensive eye examinations with optic nerve assessment and IOP measurement are essential for early detection.

items: Several conditions straddle the boundary between ophthalmology and neurology, and their management often requires collaboration — which is uniquely available at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care where Dr. Dibya Prabha (Ophthalmology) and Dr. Yuvraj Lahre (Neurology) practice under the same roof.

In Palamu: Optic neuritis — inflammation of the optic nerve, often the first manifestation of multiple sclerosis — presents with subacute, painful vision loss (worse with eye movement), reduced color vision (desaturation), and a relative afferent pupillary defect.

Ischemic optic neuropathy (anterior — AION, and posterior — PION) causes sudden, painless vision loss from infarction of the optic nerve head, with non-arteritic AION associated with vascular risk factors and a crowded optic disc, and arteritic AION from giant cell arteritis requiring emergency high-dose steroids.

Papilledema — bilateral optic disc swelling from raised intracranial pressure — demands urgent brain imaging to rule out a mass lesion and, if negative, measurement of CSF opening pressure and evaluation for idiopathic intracranial hypertension.

Cranial nerve palsies affecting eye movements — third nerve (oculomotor — ptosis, down-and-out eye, possible pupil involvement indicating a PCOM aneurysm), fourth nerve (trochlear — vertical diplopia), and sixth nerve (abducens — horizontal diplopia) — require neurological workup including MRI.
Thyroid eye disease (Graves' ophthalmopathy) causes proptosis, eyelid retraction, restrictive strabismus, and compressive optic neuropathy.

Eyelid conditions — ptosis (drooping eyelid), entropion and ectropion (inward or outward turning), and eyelid tumors (basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, sebaceous gland carcinoma) — complete the spectrum.
The co-location of ophthalmology and neurology at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care ensures that patients with neuro-ophthalmic conditions receive seamless, integrated care from both specialists.

faqs.question: What is the most common cause of blindness that is preventable?
faqs.answer: Diabetic retinopathy is the leading cause of preventable blindness in working-age adults (aged 20 to 65) worldwide. The tragedy is that severe vision loss from diabetic retinopathy is almost entirely preventable with: (1) tight blood sugar and blood pressure control, which reduces the risk of developing retinopathy by up to 75 percent and slows progression of existing disease; (2) annual dilated eye examinations, which detect retinopathy in its asymptomatic, treatable stages — laser treatment at the right time reduces the risk of severe vision loss by over 90 percent; and (3) timely treatment with intravitreal anti-VEGF injections for diabetic macular edema and pan-retinal photocoagulation for proliferative retinopathy. Yet, a significant proportion of diabetics do not get annual eye exams, and retinopathy remains a leading cause of blindness. On a global scale, cataract is the leading cause of reversible blindness — but it is fully curable with a 15-minute surgery. Dr. Dibya Prabha emphasizes that a dilated eye examination for every diabetic, every year, is the most impactful public health measure for preventing diabetes-related blindness. Our team at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care is dedicated to providing these advanced services locally in Medininagar, Jharkhand.

faqs.question: Can lifestyle and diet really prevent eye conditions, or is it mostly genetic?
faqs.answer: Both genetics and lifestyle play significant roles in eye disease, and lifestyle modifications can substantially reduce risk even in genetically predisposed individuals. The Age-Related Eye Disease Study (AREDS and AREDS2) provided Level 1 evidence that a specific combination of antioxidants (vitamin C, vitamin E, lutein, zeaxanthin, and zinc) slows the progression of moderate to advanced age-related macular degeneration by approximately 25 percent. Smoking is the strongest modifiable risk factor for AMD, increasing risk 2- to 4-fold. UV protection (sunglasses and hats) reduces the risk of cataract and pterygium. Tight blood sugar and blood pressure control in diabetes dramatically reduces the risk and progression of diabetic retinopathy. A Mediterranean-style diet rich in green leafy vegetables, fatty fish, nuts, and fruits is protective for AMD and dry eye. Regular aerobic exercise reduces intraocular pressure and improves ocular blood flow. For conditions like glaucoma, family history is a strong risk factor, but early detection through regular screening and IOP-lowering treatment can prevent vision loss even in genetically high-risk individuals. Dr. Dibya Prabha provides individualized lifestyle and nutritional counseling at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care.

faqs.question: What should I do if I am diagnosed with an eye condition that cannot be cured, like glaucoma or macular degeneration?
faqs.answer: A diagnosis of a chronic, incurable eye condition is understandably frightening, but it is important to understand that 'incurable' does not mean 'untreatable' — and most patients with these conditions maintain functional vision and quality of life with modern treatment. For glaucoma, the goal is to halt or slow progression through sustained IOP reduction — the vast majority of patients treated appropriately will not go blind from glaucoma. With medication compliance (daily eye drops) and regular monitoring (IOP checks, optic nerve imaging, and visual field testing), vision can often be preserved for a lifetime. For dry age-related macular degeneration, monitoring with an Amsler grid at home for early detection of conversion to wet AMD, AREDS2 nutritional supplementation, and UV protection are the cornerstones. For wet AMD, regular intravitreal anti-VEGF injections (typically every 4 to 12 weeks) stabilize and often improve vision. For diabetic retinopathy, strict metabolic control and regular monitoring and treatment are highly effective. For retinitis pigmentosa, low-vision rehabilitation, orientation and mobility training, and genetic counseling maximize quality of life. The key is: do not despair and do not disengage from care. Dr. Dibya Prabha walks with her patients through the journey, providing honest information, the full range of treatment options, and hope grounded in evidence — not false promises. Our team at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care is dedicated to providing these advanced services locally in Medininagar, Jharkhand.

faqs.question: When should I see a retina specialist specifically, rather than a general ophthalmologist?
faqs.answer: A retina specialist is an ophthalmologist who has completed an additional 1 to 2 years of fellowship training focused exclusively on diseases of the retina, vitreous, and macula — the most visually critical and technically demanding area of ophthalmology. You should see a retina specialist like Dr. Dibya Prabha for: (1) any condition affecting the macula — macular degeneration (dry or wet), diabetic macular edema, macular hole, epiretinal membrane, or central serous chorioretinopathy, (2) diabetic retinopathy, especially if there is macular edema, proliferative disease, or vitreous hemorrhage, (3) retinal detachment, retinal tears, or posterior vitreous detachment with high-risk features, (4) retinal vascular occlusions — central or branch retinal vein occlusion, or retinal artery occlusion, (5) unexplained vision loss where the cause is not apparent on routine examination, (6) need for intravitreal injections (anti-VEGF or steroids), retinal laser, or vitrectomy surgery, and (7) intraocular tumors (choroidal melanoma, retinoblastoma, choroidal metastasis). Dr. Dibya Prabha's fellowship training at LV Prasad Eye Institute Hyderabad — one of India's premier retina centers — gives her specialized expertise in these complex conditions, and she provides comprehensive medical and laser retina care at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, Palamu.

sections.heading: Symptoms That Should Prompt a Retina Evaluation

items: Certain visual symptoms are red flags for retinal pathology and should prompt a dilated retinal examination by a retina specialist, not just a general eye check. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

In Palamu: Sudden onset of flashes of light in the peripheral vision (especially when triggered by eye movement in dim light) and a new shower of floaters (dots, cobwebs, or a ring) — classic warning signs of posterior vitreous detachment with a 10 to 15 percent risk of an associated retinal tear, which can progress to retinal detachment.
A dark curtain, shadow, or veil that appears in any part of the peripheral vision and progressively enlarges — the cardinal symptom of retinal detachment.
Sudden, painless, severe loss of vision in one eye — a retinal artery occlusion (eye stroke) or vitreous hemorrhage.
Straight lines appearing wavy, bent, or broken (metamorphopsia) — the hallmark of macular disease (wet AMD, diabetic macular edema, macular hole, or epiretinal membrane).
A dark or missing spot in the central vision — a macular hole or severe macular degeneration.
Gradual, progressive constriction of the peripheral visual field with night blindness — retinitis pigmentosa or other inherited retinal dystrophies.
Any vision change in a patient with diabetes — diabetic retinopathy can progress silently; do not wait for symptoms to become severe.
Distortion of central vision where objects appear smaller (micropsia) or larger (macropsia) in one eye — central serous chorioretinopathy or epiretinal membrane.

content.title: Do not wait

sections.heading: Conditions That Require Retina Specialist Care

items: Several retinal conditions absolutely require the expertise of a retina specialist for optimal outcomes: At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

In Palamu: Diabetic retinopathy — especially if there is diabetic macular edema (requiring anti-VEGF injections or steroid implants), proliferative diabetic retinopathy (requiring pan-retinal photocoagulation laser), or vitreous hemorrhage (which may require vitrectomy).

Age-related macular degeneration — wet AMD requires urgent anti-VEGF injections to prevent irreversible central vision loss; dry AMD with geographic atrophy requires monitoring for conversion to wet AMD and AREDS2 nutritional supplementation.

Retinal detachment — a surgical emergency where the surgery (vitrectomy, scleral buckle, pneumatic retinopexy, or a combination) is technically demanding and must be tailored to the specific characteristics of the detachment.
Macular hole — a full-thickness defect in the central retina requiring vitrectomy with internal limiting membrane peeling and gas tamponade.
Epiretinal membrane (macular pucker) — when visually significant, requires vitrectomy and membrane peeling.
Retinal vein occlusion — branch or central, with macular edema requiring anti-VEGF injections or steroid implants, and retinal ischemia requiring laser.
Intraocular tumors — choroidal melanoma, choroidal metastasis, and retinoblastoma require retina specialist evaluation for diagnosis and management.
High myopia with retinal pathology — lattice degeneration, myopic macular degeneration, choroidal neovascularization, and retinal detachment risk.
Ocular trauma with retinal or vitreous involvement.
Complicated post-cataract surgery conditions — retained lens fragments, cystoid macular edema, endophthalmitis, and retinal detachment.

Dr. Dibya Prabha's fellowship training at LV Prasad Eye Institute Hyderabad covers the full spectrum of medical, laser, and surgical retina care. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

sections.heading: What Happens During a Retina Examination

items: A retina examination at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care is comprehensive and systematic. Here is what to expect:

In Palamu: Detailed history — Dr. Dibya Prabha begins with a detailed history focusing on: the specific visual symptom, its onset, duration, and progression, associated symptoms (flashes, floaters, pain, headache), and medical history (diabetes, hypertension, autoimmune disease, medications, and family history of retinal disease).
Visual acuity — checked with your current glasses and with a pinhole to separate refractive from retinal causes of vision loss.
Amsler grid — used to detect metamorphopsia (distortion) and scotomas.

Pupil dilation — the pupils are dilated with eye drops that take 20 to 30 minutes for full effect. You will have light sensitivity and blurred near vision for 3 to 4 hours afterward, so bring sunglasses and arrange for someone to drive you home.
Slit lamp biomicroscopy — once dilated, Dr. Prabha uses a 78D or 90D lens to obtain a magnified, stereoscopic view of the macula, optic nerve, and retinal vessels.

Indirect ophthalmoscopy with scleral depression — used to examine the peripheral retina out to the ora serrata, the far periphery where retinal tears most commonly occur. This is the single most important part of the examination for flashes and floaters.

Optical coherence tomography (OCT) — provides a high-resolution, microscopic cross-section of the macula, revealing edema, subretinal fluid, drusen, holes, membranes, and atrophy. It is the most powerful diagnostic tool for macular disease.
OCT angiography (OCTA) — visualizes retinal and choroidal blood flow without dye injection.
Fundus photography — documents the appearance of the retina for serial comparison.
Fluorescein angiography — when needed, maps retinal circulation and identifies leakage, ischemia, and neovascularization.

After synthesizing all findings, Dr. Prabha explains the diagnosis, answers your questions, and outlines a treatment plan tailored to your specific condition — all in clear, understandable terms. faqs.question: How often do I need retina follow-up if I have a chronic condition like diabetic retinopathy or macular degeneration?
faqs.answer: The follow-up interval is individualized based on your specific condition, severity, treatment regimen, and response. For stable, mild non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy without macular edema: every 6 to 12 months. For diabetic macular edema on anti-VEGF injections: typically every 4 to 6 weeks initially, with the interval extended based on treatment response (treat-and-extend protocol). For wet AMD on anti-VEGF injections: typically every 4 to 12 weeks depending on the specific drug and regimen. For a retinal tear treated with laser: a follow-up examination in 1 to 2 weeks to confirm an adequate laser scar, then monitoring as needed. For a posterior vitreous detachment with no tear found on initial examination: a recheck in 2 to 4 weeks to ensure no delayed tear has developed (the risk period for a retinal tear is the first 4 to 6 weeks after PVD onset). For stable dry AMD: every 6 to 12 months with Amsler grid self-monitoring at home. For high myopia: annual dilated examination. Dr. Prabha provides a clear follow-up schedule at each visit and explains the rationale behind it. Our team at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care is dedicated to providing these advanced services locally in Medininagar, Jharkhand.

faqs.question: Are intravitreal injections painful, and what are the risks?
faqs.answer: Intravitreal injections are the most common retina procedure performed worldwide, and while the idea of an injection into the eye is understandably anxiety-provoking, the procedure is quick, well-tolerated, and extremely safe when performed under proper aseptic technique. Before the injection, the eye is numbed with topical anesthetic drops (and sometimes a subconjunctival lidocaine injection for additional anesthesia), and the surface is sterilized with povidone-iodine 5% to minimize infection risk. A speculum keeps the eye open. The injection itself takes less than a second, and most patients feel only mild pressure, not sharp pain. The entire procedure takes under 5 minutes. The most feared complication is endophthalmitis — a severe intraocular infection — which occurs in approximately 1 in 2,000 to 1 in 5,000 injections when strict aseptic protocol is followed. Other risks include: subconjunctival hemorrhage (a painless patch of blood on the white of the eye that resolves in 1 to 2 weeks — very common and harmless), temporary floaters from the drug or a small air bubble, transiently elevated intraocular pressure, and retinal detachment or tear (rare). Dr. Dibya Prabha follows rigorous aseptic protocol, uses povidone-iodine antisepsis, and monitors patients after each injection. The benefits — preventing irreversible central vision loss from wet AMD or diabetic macular edema — vastly outweigh the small procedural risks. Our team at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care is dedicated to providing these advanced services locally in Medininagar, Jharkhand.

faqs.question: Can retinal detachment be treated without surgery?
faqs.answer: Some retinal detachments can be treated with less invasive in-office procedures, but most established retinal detachments require surgery. The specific treatment depends on the type, location, size, and duration of the detachment. A retinal tear without detachment — the precursor to retinal detachment — is treated in the office with laser retinopexy (creating burns around the tear to seal it) or cryopexy (freezing treatment). This is quick, effective, and prevents the progression to detachment. For a small, localized retinal detachment confined to the peripheral retina and not involving the macula, pneumatic retinopexy may be an option: a gas bubble is injected into the vitreous cavity, and the patient is positioned so the bubble rises and tamponades the retinal break, allowing the subretinal fluid to pump out. Laser or cryopexy is then applied. This is an in-office or minor procedure and avoids the need for a full vitrectomy in selected cases. However, most retinal detachments — especially those that are larger, involve the macula, or have multiple or large breaks — require surgical repair by pars plana vitrectomy (removing the vitreous gel, draining subretinal fluid, applying laser around the breaks, and filling the eye with gas or silicone oil) or scleral buckling (placing a silicone band around the outside of the eye to indent the wall and close the break). The surgical approach is tailored to the individual detachment characteristics. The most important determinant of final visual outcome is whether the macula is attached at the time of surgery — which is why you must seek care urgently when you notice the symptoms of retinal detachment. Dr. Dibya Prabha provides same-day evaluation and coordinates surgical repair without delay.
